content.text:
**Do not accept the combined slices yet: 0032 still produces reproducible one-pulse release errors.** The 96-case cadence matrix passes, and 0033 fixes replacement ownership in my focused reproduction; reentrant Stop still crashes, but that failure predates these patches.

- **0032: wrapped parent phase loses the release origin.** With parent period **24 pulses**, zero spread, arp division **1/24**, and an eight-step gate, the note starting at pulse **23 releases at 25**, instead of **24**; this repeats at 47→49. The parent has already wrapped to phase 1 before the arp callback, so `math.max(0, (parent.phase - 2) / parent.current_ppqn)` produces zero ([m_clock.lua:619](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_clock.lua:619)). Wrapping occurs at [m_lattice.lua:525](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_lattice.lua:525). Preserve the actual onset position across that wrap; simply allowing a negative offset is insufficient because a resulting zero length executes immediately ([m_clock.lua:531](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_clock.lua:531)).

- **0032: floating-point addition moves exact deadlines.** With parent period **216**, division **1/24**, zero spread, and an eight-step gate, onset **54 releases at 64**, instead of **63**. I reproduced this using the actual `step.lua` release helper and clock/lattice code. Adding duration and phase offset ([step.lua:455](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/step.lua:455)) creates a deadline infinitesimally above an integer; the strict comparison waits another pulse ([m_lattice.lua:222](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_lattice.lua:222)). Normalize near-integer pulse deadlines without changing the established pending-time policy.

- **0033: replacement ownership works in the focused reproduction.** An old generation ending at pulse 24 releases only its own pending note; the replacement’s note survives until its gate at 72. With HEAD’s clock implementation, both release at 24. The candidate removes each owned pending action before invoking it ([m_clock.lua:600](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_clock.lua:600)). Same-pitch receiver behavior remains the existing overlap policy: MIDI emits every corresponding Note Off ([m_midi.lua:301](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/m_midi.lua:301)); generation-local IDs do not imply independent receiver voices.

- **Preexisting, still uncovered: reentrant Stop crashes.** Calling `m_clock:stop()` once from the old generation’s gate-triggered release callback produces `m_lattice.lua:164: attempt to index a nil value`. Stop destroys the lattice while its pulse iterator continues ([m_clock.lua:834](<mosaic-worktree>/lib/clock/m_clock.lua:834)). Repeating with HEAD’s clock implementation also crashes. A narrow iterator/lifecycle guard is the correction direction; this is not a newly introduced 0033 defect.

Before acceptance, add exact release/order assertions for both counterexamples, plus replacement using identical pitches, another channel with a pending release, and reentrant Stop with multiple owned releases. Add fractional-rate and mid-interval faster/slower rate-change cases against the retained pending-time reference. Current native arp cases exercise half-step spacing ([cases.py:1023](<mosaic-worktree>/tests/behaviour/cases.py:1023)); the 96-case matrix checks cadence, not releases.

**CONFIDENCE: High** for these reproductions; I did not verify the running candidate matrix’s final result. Nonzero spread semantics and overall manual/full-release acceptance remain incomplete.
